extracted.intended_audience: NLP / ML researchers and developers building automated peer-review / author-feedback systems; researchers studying automated review evaluation
extracted.subtask_description: Generate structured, actionable pre-submission feedback for academic papers (summary, strengths, weaknesses, questions) using retrieval and LLMs, with passage selection via graph neural networks and evaluation via automatic and human judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structured feedback fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Generate structured, actionable pre-submission feedback containing Summary, Strengths, Weaknesses, and Questions, without producing acceptance recommendations or replacing human peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The system's output should include the four fields (Summary, Strengths, Weaknesses, Questions). Exclude rating-based fields that correspond to final decision-making (e.g., accept/reject, score). Use the Summary, Strengths, Weaknesses, and Questions sections of human-written peer reviews as supervision signals (GPT-4 consolidated reviews used in training).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of peer reviews as proxy supervision
rubrics_metrics.description: In the absence of large-scale pre-submission feedback datasets, use human-written peer reviews as a proxy; retain only Summary, Strengths, Weaknesses, and Questions as supervision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justification: peer reviews provide expert critiques aligned with guidance authors seek pre-submission. Caveat: reviews reflect variable writing maturity and reviewer focus. Support choice with user study when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passage segmentation policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Segment each paper into discrete passages split at newline characters (\n); for DPR queries, concatenate k consecutive sentences (k ∈ {1,3,5}) to form a single query.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each passage is a candidate context. For each query (concatenated k sentences), retrieve the top-m most relevant passages (m ∈ {3,5}) using DPR. Consolidate unique passages retrieved across multiple queries per paper to form training labels for the GNN.

rubrics_metrics.name: DPR retrieval configuration
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Dense Passage Retrieval (DPR) to identify passages corresponding to feedback sections, retrieving top-m passages per query based on semantic similarity in embedding space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete choices used: multiset-base DPR context and question encoders; m ∈ {3,5}; k ∈ {1,3,5}. Retrieved passages across varied k,m serve as ground truth labels for training the GNN. DPR is a baseline but may miss some key passages that graph-based methods recover.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document graph construction (nodes & edges)
rubrics_metrics.description: Represent each paper as an undirected hierarchical document graph G = (V,E) with nodes for the paper root, section headings, sub-headings, passages, and sentences; edges encode hierarchical links (Ehier) and sequential links (Eseq).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ehier reflects structural nesting; Eseq preserves linear ordering of passages and sentences. The union E = Ehier ∪ Eseq enables vertical propagation and lateral flow. Graph construction is agnostic to section depth and adapts to nested structures. Full node/edge definitions provided in Appendix A (paper).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigate over-squashing via rewiring (sequential edges)
rubrics_metrics.description: Augment the hierarchical backbone with sequential edges to facilitate lateral information flow and reduce over-squashing/bottlenecks in tree-like graphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: hierarchical trees can concentrate neighbor information at root leading to information bottlenecks; sequential edges (e.g., passage-to-next-passage, sentence-to-next-sentence) preserve textual progression and reduce dependence on deep hierarchical paths. Expect typical graph depth ≤ 5 hops for scientific papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: GNN-based passage selection (training objective)
rubrics_metrics.description: Train a Graph Attention Network (GAT) over the document graph to classify passage nodes as feedback-relevant or not, using DPR-extracted passages as ground-truth labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Node embeddings for sentence nodes initialized with Sentence-Transformer all-mpnet-base-v2; other node types initialized as zero embeddings (dim=768). Trained models are denoted GNN(k,m) corresponding to DPR parameters used to create labels. Use binary classification loss (Cross Entropy) and retain best validation checkpoint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passage selection operational advantage
rubrics_metrics.description: At inference time, the GNN autonomously identifies salient passages directly from the document graph, eliminating dependence on human-generated feedback as queries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach reduces the need for external grounding and lowers input context length for LLMs, improving both factual grounding and computational efficiency relative to full-text approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context length minimization for LLM input
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduce LLM input token length by selecting a subset of salient passages to improve generation quality and efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical evidence: average token lengths reported for Full Paper (~9446 tokens) vs GNN (5,5) (~4147 tokens) and GNN (5,3) (~2899 tokens). Shorter contexts improve LLM performance (reference Hsieh et al., 2024). Choose configuration (k,m) to balance context richness vs training/inference cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM fine-tuning objective and input format
rubrics_metrics.description: Fine-tune LLMs on GNN-selected passages with supervision targets consisting of the four structured fields; prompts should instruct the model to output Summary, Strengths, Weaknesses, and Questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example prompt template (used in finetuning): Instruction + Research Paper Passages + 'Feedback for the paper:' followed by **Summary**, **Strengths**, **Weaknesses**, **Questions**. Fine-tuning used LoRA (rank=8, α=16) for efficiency and 3 epochs in experiments; apply LoRA to q_proj,k_proj,v_proj,o_proj and other transformer matrices as listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not issue acceptance recommendations or final decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The system must avoid producing acceptance/rejection recommendations or ratings that correspond to final decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design intent: author-centric pre-submission aid, not a reviewer replacement. Exclude rating-based fields from training targets and outputs to prevent misuse as a decision tool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic evaluation metrics for feedback quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate generated structured feedback using ROUGE-1/2/L (Recall and F1), BERTScore-F1, and Aspect Coverage (ACov) to assess lexical overlap, semantic similarity, and breadth of aspects covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ROUGE measures surface overlap (use both Recall and F1); BERTScore-F1 assesses semantic similarity; Aspect Coverage (Yuan et al., 2022) measures whether feedback engages with diverse scholarly dimensions beyond summarization. Use stemming options consistently when computing ROUGE for reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aspect Coverage dimensions (ACov aspects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure breadth of scholarly criteria addressed by feedback across aspects: Summary (SUM), Clarity (CLA), Soundness/Correctness (SOU), Substance (SUB), Originality (ORI), Meaningful Comparison (CMP), Replicability (REP), Motivation/Impact (MOT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report per-aspect coverage percentages. Use an aspect tagger (e.g., Yuan et al., 2022) to compute ACov and identify dimensions where feedback is weak (e.g., Motivation/Impact, Replicability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Human qualitative assessment categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess generated feedback along four qualitative dimensions: Feedback Depth (FD), Feedback Thoroughness (FT), Feedback Constructiveness (FC), Feedback Helpfulness (FH), using a 1–5 scale with explicit level definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Definitions (excerpted):
- FD: technical understanding and meaningful engagement (1 Unqualified to 5 Authoritative).
- FT: coverage of methodology/results/reproducibility (1 Negligent to 5 Forensic).
- FC: utility of suggestions (1 Destructive to 5 Transformative).
- FH: effectiveness of issue identification and explanation (1 Misleading to 5 Revelatory).
Annotators should be eligible domain experts; each feedback annotated by multiple annotators (paper used 3 annotators per feedback) and scores averaged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring methodology for qualitative categories (human / LLM-as-judge)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each qualitative category, find highest level (5–1) where ALL criteria are fully satisfied (Base Level). Then check Base+1 level to compute partial credit as (Satisfied criteria in higher level / Total criteria in higher level). Final score = Base Level + Partial Credit, rounded to two decimals (specific rounding increments given).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedure was provided in Appendix E / Figure 4 for both human annotators and LLM-as-a-Judge prompts; use it to enable partial-credit scoring across multi-criteria definitions per level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factual validity assessment rubric (per-claim)
rubrics_metrics.description: Annotate each discrete claim in feedback for factual consistency with the source paper using four labels: Completely Agree, Mostly Agree, Mostly Disagree, Completely Disagree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural rules: read the entire paper first; treat the entire Summary as one discrete claim; treat each bulleted point in Strengths/Weaknesses/Questions as a discrete claim. Definitions: Completely Agree = entirely accurate; Mostly Agree = mostly correct with minor gaps; Mostly Disagree = mostly incorrect; Completely Disagree = factually wrong or hallucinated. Use dropdown scales and provide per-claim judgments; aggregate percentages (e.g., CA/MA = positive rating).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotator eligibility and annotation protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure annotators conducting qualitative and factual assessments are eligible to review for the target conference (domain experts); use multiple annotators per item and average results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experimental setup used 27 annotators for qualitative assessment (3 annotations per feedback) and 10 annotators for factual validity (each paper evaluated by 2 annotators). Use a UI that displays the full paper and the feedback (Streamlit in the paper).

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM-as-a-Judge as scalable proxy
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a large LLM (e.g., Gemini-2.0-Flash) prompted with the qualitative assessment guidelines as an automated judge to approximate human preferences at scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt human prompts for LLM-as-a-Judge; validate correlation between automated judge scores and human annotations before trusting large-scale judgments. The paper reports strong correlation in their experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ablation and hyperparameter trade-offs (k,m)
rubrics_metrics.description: Vary k (number of review sentences concatenated: 1,3,5) and m (number of top DPR-retrieved passages used to train the GNN: 3,5) to study effect on feedback quality and training cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finding: increasing k and m provides richer context leading to consistent improvements on metrics, but increases training time and computational cost. Choose (k,m) for an efficiency-performance trade-off (e.g., Llama (5,3) reduces training time with minor performance loss vs (5,5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Passage classifier / GNN implementation & training standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a Graph Attention Network (GAT) with multiple GATConv layers, residual connections, activations, dropout; followed by an MLP passage classifier; train for sufficient epochs (the paper used 30 epochs) and use Cross Entropy loss.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation details: initialize sentence node embeddings with all-mpnet-base-v2 (dim=768), other nodes zero; first GATConv maps to 128-d per head with 4 heads (concatenated), residual projections, ELU and dropout p=0.2; further layers as described; classifier MLP uses SiLU activations, dropout p=0.3, layernorm; retain best validation checkpoint for inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fine-tuning hyperparameter choices for LLM adaptation
rubrics_metrics.description: When fine-tuning LLMs for structured feedback, apply Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) for parameter-efficient tuning and choose sensible hyperparameters (e.g., LoRA rank=8, α=16, 3 epochs, learning rate 1e-4, AdamW optimizer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate LoRA into q_proj, k_proj, v_proj, o_proj, gate_proj, up_proj, down_proj. Use FP16 training, gradient accumulation / batch sizes as hardware permits. Report training time to reflect efficiency-performance trade-offs across configurations and models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation reporting standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Report both automatic metrics (ROUGE F1/Recall, BERTScore-F1) and human evaluation results (qualitative scores, factual validity percentages, impact survey responses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include training/test split sizes, model configuration labels (e.g., Mistral (k,m), Llama (k,m)), and compute Aspect Coverage by aspect. Report human evaluation sample sizes and annotator counts, and aggregate results (means, percentages).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical and deployment considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge risks of bias, misuse, and academic integrity; design system as a supplementary author-centric aid and advocate for transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose training data provenance (e.g., historical peer reviews consolidated by GPT-4) and possible biases (leniency toward well-known authors, under-representation of areas). Warn against over-reliance, potential misuse for decision-making, and risks of academic misconduct (e.g., misrepresenting AI critiques as human). Recommend transparency and supplementary use only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factual evaluation procedural guideline (claim extraction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure for factual validity annotation: read full paper, identify every discrete claim in feedback, treat Summary as one claim and each bullet in Strengths/Weaknesses/Questions as separate claims, then rate each claim on 1–4 validity scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This stepwise process ensures consistent per-claim judgments and reduces ambiguity about unit of annotation. Provide annotators with explicit dropdown categories and examples; use aggregated per-claim statistics (CA/MA/MD/CD) to quantify grounding and hallucination rates.
